So, $SPY V-bottom or W-bottom?

After $SPY declined roughly 6% toward $732, I deployed 25% of my Blood in the Street Account into long-term positions.

The subsequent snapback created excellent trading opportunities, but the rally has now encountered resistance around $763, another lower high near the previous breakdown.

The critical levels are $753 and Friday's $747 low. If buyers defend these areas, the market could establish a constructive W-shaped bottom before attempting another move higher.

With very few constructive stock setups and limited leadership, I remain cautious about the sustainability of the rebound.

$NVDA earnings this week could be a major rurning point.

Nvidia has suffered a nearly 40% correction from approximately $240 to $148, where a hammer-like reversal and strong volume triggered a sharp rebound.

I see $158, Friday's low, as the immediate level to watch.

Holding it could create another tactical opportunity, potentially even a red-to-green reversal. Losing it would weaken the setup.

While Nvidia may meet or beat earnings expectations and deliver strong guidance, I believe significant overhead resistance and uncertainty surrounding Jensen Huang could limit the upside.

Unlike previous 40%+ corrections that recovered within months, I doubt Nvidia will reclaim its former highs anytime soon.

A post-earnings bounce may be tradable, but that doesn't necessarily mean the longer-term damage has been repaired.

*

ANTHROPIC IPO: THE "ART OF THE FIRST DAY" $ANT

I discussed so many times how I approach major IPOs using a strategy developed over two decades.

Rather than chasing hype, I watch the opening print, the first five-minute candle, and the initial trading range.

If buyers establish control and the stock breaks above its opening range, opportunities can emerge. If it cannot even reclaim its opening price, I prefer to stay away.

$SPCX and $CRBS were a great recent examples.

I would even consider some $TSLL exposure in case the rumored transaction materializes.

*

Bottom line: this week could determine whether the market's recovery gains credibility or turns into another selling opportunity.

Watch the levels above, respect the risks, and remember: a powerful snapback is not the same as a repaired market!

$SPY has reclaimed $738 and turned from red to green, potentially establishing a higher low above $732.

A successful reclaim of $660 could create an attractive oversold bounce and potentially establish a higher low.

$NVDA is the next major catalyst, with earnings due after today's close.

Following its dramatic decline from $243 to $148, I believe a short-term bounce is possible toward $158 and potentially $163.

Despite challenging short-term trading, including Monday's abrupt reversal from $140 to $136 after a strong session, I believe #SPCX will be a major long-term survivor and trade substantially higher over time.

I see this resilience as an encouraging sign that #TSLA could outperform if the broader market stabilizes.

The V failed. Now the question is whether a W-shaped bottom can finally put the market back on solid ground.

THE MARKET'S LAST CHANCE FOR A BOUNCE + WHY I'M HOLDING MOSTLY CASH + WHY SELL RULES MATTER + $NVDA GREEN-TO-RED? + $SPCX / $TSLA RELATIVE STRENGTH

The next two trading sessions are critical. Following $NVDA earnings, AI, semiconductor, and growth stocks remain under pressure, while $SPY and $QQQ are attempting to establish a double bottom near their November 5 lows.

This could be the market's last chance to build a meaningful oversold rally into Thanksgiving.

*

Last week, I expected the V-shaped recovery to turn into a W, with a retest of the November 5 lows. That's exactly what happened.

$SPY rallied from $732 to $762, delivering a tremendous 30-point move, before stalling, breaking $753, and returning toward $732.

Now down roughly 7% from its highs, #SPY has potentially formed a double-bottom undercut, shaking out stops before reclaiming support.

$QQQ has a similar setup, retesting its $647 low without undercutting it. But holding support isn't enough.

#QQQ must reclaim yesterday's $663 high, followed by $667 and $671. For SPY, watch $738, $741, $744, and $747.

If buyers can't push these indexes away from their lows, another leg lower becomes increasingly likely.

*

$NVDA is the catalyst today.

Earnings guidance and CUDA commentary were encouraging, but concerns remain about Jensen's testimony, leadership uncertainty, and broader AI weakness.

#NVDA needs to reclaim and HOLD $158 to potentially reach $163 and its 8-day moving average. If it opens $4–$5 higher and turns red, that's a serious warning that sellers remain in control.

Anthropic's $ANT anticipated debut adds another catalyst this week.

If #Nvidia holds its gains, Anthropic performs well, and the indexes reclaim resistance, we could see a Thanksgiving rally. If these catalysts fail, the market could face another difficult stretch.

*

WHY AM I HOLDING MOSTLY CASH?

If you remember, I've deployed only one tier of my Blood in the Street Account because I want flexibility if 2027 becomes much more challenging.

Political uncertainty, potentially less corporation-friendly policies, and a slowdown in AI spending are real risks.

I'm not predicting disaster, but I'm not getting fully invested just because stocks have fallen.

*

And remember why SELL RULES matter.

Look at $NBIS. An incredible trend carried it toward $299 before it collapsed through $232 and eventually toward $100.

Investors who ignored the 8/21-day moving averages and convinced themselves it was heading to $500 are now trapped. Great stories don't protect you from devastating drawdowns.

*

I'm still finding selective opportunities, though not that many.

I've bought substantial $SPCX over the past two sessions and trimmed some into strength. It's holding up technically better than many growth names.

$TSLA is also showing relative strength, remaining well above its November 5 lows while QQQ retested its own.

*

So, my strategy right now: respect the sell rules, preserve cash, favor relative strength, and stay tactical.

If the double bottom holds, there's an opportunity. If it fails, I'm prepared to get defensive again.

Patience and capital preservation come first.

📺 ANTHROPIC IPO WILL IGNITE A MASSIVE MARKET RALLY? + THE ART OF THE FIRST DAY – $ANT SETUP + $SPY & $QQQ FORM W-BOTTOMS + $SPCX & $TSLA UPDATES

With $SPX futures surging 95 points and $SPY indicating a $9 gap higher toward $739, the market is staging an impressive comeback.

But is this the beginning of a sustainable recovery or another temporary bounce?

After falling roughly 7% from its highs, $SPY formed an initial V-bottom, retested its lows with a slight undercut, and developed a potential W-bottom.

The next major test is the 8-day moving average near $743, which has repeatedly rejected price.

*

$QQQ looks even stronger, jumping approximately $11 premarket and reclaiming its 8-day moving average.

Its recent double-bottom formation provided an early clue that selling pressure might be exhausting.

The key question now: how much of this massive opening gap can the market hold?

*

While $QQQ retested its November 5 lows, both $SPCX and $TSLA held higher lows, demonstrating relative strength.

That divergence gave me a compelling reason to maintain active swing positions despite the broader correction.

I continued buying $SPCX on pullbacks throughout this week, maintaining both shares and options exposure.

With $SPCX gaining approximately 2.7% premarket, my strategy is paying off. I plan to trim some profits while keeping a portion of the position.

The lesson? Look for stocks that refuse to make new lows when the broader market does. Those are often the names that lead when buying returns.

*

$ANT IPO: THE ART OF THE FIRST DAY

I talk a lot about my 20+ year IPO trading framework, emphasizing why traders should NEVER blindly chase the opening print.

My strategy revolves around the opening five-minute high.

Using a hypothetical $ANT offering price of $83 and an opening at $90, suppose shares initially rally to $92 before pulling back.

Early institutional investors who received allocations at $83 may sell to lock in quick profits, creating substantial supply.

Rather than buying immediately, I wait for that selling pressure to clear.

If $ANT subsequently breaks above $92, it signals that buyers have absorbed the supply, potentially opening the door to $93, $94, and $95.

But if shares fail to reclaim $92 and instead fall toward $89–$88, I would stay away.

We saw $SPCX's successful IPO breakout from $176 toward $192 and eventually $225, versus $CBRS, which failed to sustain its opening strength and subsequently collapsed.

*

Bottom line: #Anthropic could provide the catalyst for a powerful market rebound, but the opening excitement alone isn't a buy signal.

Let $ANT's opening-range breakout confirm genuine demand. Also watch whether $SPY and $QQQ hold their gaps.

Trade the confirmation, not the hype.

**Mid-Day Brief — Thu Nov 19** (as of ~12:45pm ET)

**Tape**
● S&P ~7,250 (-1.0%), Nasdaq ~24,260 (-0.7%), Dow ~49,440 (-1.5%) — sixth straight down day for the S&P if it holds
● SPY $722.44 (-1.1%) — day range $717.54–$739.90 — 7.6% off its $781.62 high
● QQQ $653.68 (-0.9%) — day range $647.16–$676.49 — 14.3% off its $762.86 high
● SMH $454.88 (-1.0%) — day range $447.82–$479.96 — 32.3% off its $671.83 high
● ANT (IPO day 1) — opened $111.50, high $115.10, low $96.50, last ~$100 (+~21% vs the $83 IPO price)
● VIX ~28; 10Y ~5.06%; Bitcoin ~$62,900

**What's happening**
● The major indices opened strong before aggressively fading — the Nasdaq-100 opened up nearly 2% and SPY ran +1.3% at the high; both have round-tripped red
● The slump has set off a scramble of headline searching, but it's a futile exercise — you didn't miss anything. The excuses making the rounds: the Fed is hawkish, Trump might bomb Iran, retail earnings were blah, the new chip export rules are already negatively impacting sales into China, AMD might have an Nvidia/China-like problem of its own according to Hunterbrook, the Philadelphia Fed report for November was bad, the gov't might shut down next month, cybersecurity risks are mounting
● What's really happening feels more technical than anything else — people just don't have much enthusiasm for this market, and rallies tend to bring out sellers instead of chasers. There's still a lot of hesitation when it comes to being long AI-linked names, especially picks-and-shovels, and the defensive stuff is quite extended after the recent rally

**Drivers**
● Philly Fed fell to 6.3 vs ~20 expected (from 20.9) — a six-month low, new orders negative at -0.4 — and prices paid jumped to 58.2 from 43.2: growth cools, prices heat up
● Jobless claims 203K vs ~198K expected; continuing claims 1.763M — labor cooling at the edges
● Hunterbrook hit AMD — its firmware traced to blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems and three linked sellers; AMD $486.51 (-8.2%), day low $470.56. Hunterbrook is short AMD and concedes the findings don't establish an export violation; AMD hasn't commented
● NVDA $149.37 (-1.1%) — new intraday low $147.82, under its $148.80 52-week low
● PANW $360.47 (+6.0%), high $370.00 — holding most of its earnings move; cybersecurity led tech early
● WMT $126.15 (-1.0%) — beat (adj. EPS $0.65 vs $0.64, revenue $188.8B) and raised FY guide to $2.84–$2.89, sold anyway
● All 11 sectors down; health care worst, tech holding up best

**Ahead**
● ANT into the close — whether it holds ~$100 is the afternoon's AI-sentiment read
● After the close: INTU, ROST, KEYS
● Dow watch: a -1% close today would be its fourth straight 1%+ drop
● Friday: monthly options expiration; SNDK starts trading split-adjusted

**Closing Brief — Thu Nov 19**

● S&P 500 7,175.83 (-2.02%) — sixth straight down day
● Nasdaq 23,879.20 (-2.25%)
● Dow 49,097.06 (-2.19%, -1,101 pts) — closed below 50,000

**What happened**
● Stocks attempted to rally right out of the gate, but the effort quickly faltered. There really wasn't a lot of incremental news on Thursday specifically, and many of the reasons cited for the pressure could have been said at any time in the last few weeks
● Among the more popular justifications for the ugly price action: 1) a hawkish Fed — the FOMC is guaranteed to hike on 12/9, probably again on 1/27 and maybe 3/17 too, as it tries to wrap its arms around an inflation problem that's worse than anticipated; 2) Iran uncertainty — NYT, Axios and Bloomberg all ran "Trump is considering another bombing campaign" stories, although oil took it in stride and didn't really rally, with global markets in a state of oversupply; 3) continued AI doubts — the Anthropic IPO was impressive, but the overall pool of capital available to finance data centers remains smaller than before, while incremental restrictions on chip sales to China are already having an impact on the industry
● 4) poor economic data — the Philadelphia Fed report pointed to cooling growth and intensifying inflation; 5) US government shutdown risks — a shutdown is possible as soon as 12/11; 6) cybersecurity fears — every day brings a new wave of cyber-attack and IT-outage headlines, and they're starting to weigh on the market; 7) blah retail earnings — WMT was OK with a modest beat-and-raise, but BBWI and WSM each provided cautious guidance for Q4
● Sentiment as of the 4pm close was particularly bleak — SPX below its 200-day and sitting at multi-month lows, most people abandoning hope for a year-end rally. The midterms, Nvidia earnings and Ant's IPO don't appear to have been the clearing events many anticipated, and it's difficult to envision a catalyst to propel a dramatic turnaround, with AI-linked stuff still in the penalty box while defensives are extended and expensive
